messages.subject: Tweedie Hyperparamater
parts:
Hi

I am confusing how to show hyperparameter in my output using inla, in my model I can't see mean, sd, 0.025 quant in hyperparameter output, while I have defined the prior for parameter.
model_inla_tweedie <- inla(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
  data = data,
  family = "tweedie",  # Using Tweedie distribution for error
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config = TRUE),
  control.family = list(hyper = list(p = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(1, 0.01)))),
  control.fixed = prior.beta
)
summary(model_inla_tweedie)

Also, I am struggling to find what is the name for parameter p and phi when trying generating sample from this parameter
n_samples <- 10000
sample_tweedie <- inla.posterior.sample(n_samples, model_inla_tweedie)
posterior_linpred <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...) {Predictor}, sample_tweedie)
posterior_pred <- exp(posterior_linpred)
library(statmod)
p_posterior <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...) {p}, sample_tweedie)
phi_posterior <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...) {phi}, sample_tweedie)

there is no p and phi name, I try to find them in hyperparameter but can't get it. Please, if you mind, help me to solve this problem. Thank you

Best, 
David

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Tweedie Hyperparamater
parts:
see also inla.doc("tweedie")

here is an example

library(tweedie)
library(INLA)

n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)
eta <- 1 + x
mu <- exp(eta)

p <- 1.32
phi <- 2.0
y <- numeric(n)
for(i in 1:n) {
y[i] <- rtweedie(1, xi = p, mu = mu[i], phi = phi)
}

r <- inla(y ~ 1 + x,
data = data.frame(y, x),
family = "tweedie",
control.family = list(hyper = list(
p = list(initial = 0),
phi = list(initial = -4,
prior = "loggamma",
param = c(100, 100)))),
verbose = T)
summary(r)


then

> rownames(r$summary.hyperpar)
[1] "p parameter for Tweedie" "Dispersion parameter for Tweedie"
>


which are the names of the hyperpar of the tweedie, seee also the example code
for which 'p=' and 'phi=' which are the same names used in 'rtweedie'

for the posterior.sample.eval, you kind of need to know which indices these
parameters are located at if you have other hyperparmaeters as well, as
hyperparameters are called theta[1], theta[2], .... Note the argument 'intern'
which is default TRUE, meaning that 'theta[...]' are the user scale and not the
internal scale (like, precision and log(precision))
